Title: Replay: Record any meeting on your Mac, transcribed on-device | Product Hunt
## Record any meeting on your Mac, transcribed on-device. Replay records any meeting on your Mac (Zoom, Meet, Teams, Webex, and more) and transcribes it on-device, with speaker names it learns across meetings. Everything lands in a private, searchable Library saved as plain video, JSON, and Markdown that you own. Connect Claude in one click to ask questions in plain language and get answers cited to the exact moment. One-time purchase, no subscription. I built Replay because I was tired of the tradeoffs in every meeting notetaker: a bot joins your call, your audio gets uploaded to someone else's cloud, and you pay every month for the privilege. It records any meeting on your Mac (Zoom, Meet, Teams, and the rest) and does everything on-device: transcription and speaker separation run locally on Apple silicon. Nothing is uploaded, there is no account, and it works offline. Your recordings are saved as plain video, JSON, and Markdown that you own. Two things I am most proud of: it learns each person's voice across meetings, so transcripts already know who said what, and you can connect Claude in one click to ask questions in plain language, with every answer cited to the exact moment it was said. I would love your feedback, especially on the on-device transcription quality and the Claude integration. The on-device transcription and summaries are built on Apple's newest local frameworks (SpeechAnalyzer and Foundation Models), which only exist on macOS 26. That is the tradeoff for keeping everything local with no cloud. **You say on-device, but it connects to Claude. So the local core is private by default, and the Claude Q&A is an opt-in that uses your own Claude account. Versus the cloud tools (Otter, Granola): no bot joins your call, nothing is uploaded, it works offline, and it is one-time instead of a subscription. Replay's edge is that it records the whole meeting including video, not just audio, it learns each person's voice across meetings so speaker labels carry over from one call to the next, and it connects to Claude in one click so you can ask questions across everything you have recorded.

I love the idea, and it's really cool that you have a lifetime/pay-once option with no cloud dependency. It feels like the good old days — app purchases are back, which is possible again thanks to local AI models. Question: Can I hook my Claude Code up to the meeting transcripts to do more powerful meeting summarization? Concern: The Pay Once option only includes one year (!) of app and model updates... does that mean I'll have to buy the app again every year? @matthew\_gladyshev you absolutely can hook your Claude Code up to your meeting transcripts! The transcript and any summary Notetaker generates lives as an .md file on your computer, so you can point Claude Code to the folder with those .md files if you want to analyse/summarise them there. On Pay Once, we make sure that updates are backwards compatible, so you don't have to worry about the app stopping working. We've decided to go with a Pay Once model as we think there's no reason you should have to lock yourself into a subscription to use local models on your computer. At the same time, subscriptions and Pay Once licenses is how we fund continued development of the app (we're fully bootstrapped), so the one year of updates for the app feels like a fair and sustainable approach in our minds. So in short, you don't have to keep buying the app each year if you don't want continued updates we ship, it will continue working :). Frustrated you have to send your voice over the wire for meeting note transcriptions? Epilude transcribes and summarises your meetings on-device, on your Mac. No bot joins the call, so nobody sees an "AI Notetaker" sitting in the participant list. This has given me peace of mind when it comes to the horde of meetings each week - rather than messaging teammates and going over the same information, I can always fall back to the transcription or the locally processed AI meeting notes (yes, this all runs on your machine too).
